speakerNotes: About 2 minutes. Beat 1: 16.2M TEU (state the 14-16.2 range), point at 2028. Beat 2: MSC/COSCO 45-51% vs Hapag-Lloyd 20%. Beat 3: four drivers in one line each, then the banner. Hand-over to Req 2: fleet +9-12% a year against demand +3-6%. BIMCO 14M/42% verified: https://maritime-executive.com/article/overcapacity-looms-over-container-shipping-as-supply-pressure-mounts
headline: A record orderbook is heading for the water

carriers.title: Orderbook by carrier, M TEU (share of own fleet)
carriers.callout: MSC and COSCO are betting on scale (45–51% of their fleets on order). Hapag-Lloyd keeps a disciplined 20%.
carriers.note: Highest ratio: Wan Hai, 78%. Source: Alphaliner via El Estrecho Digital, 2026.

drivers.title: Decarbonisation rules
drivers.line: EEXI/CII, EU ETS and FuelEU make old ships dearer to run; the open IMO Net-Zero vote forces early fuel bets.

drivers.title: Economies of scale
drivers.line: About 40 megamax (~24,000 TEU) orders pending, but the cost per slot only falls when ships sail full.

drivers.title: Pandemic war chest
drivers.line: About $536bn EBIT in 2021–22 lets carriers fund newbuilds from their own cash.

drivers.title: Alliance realignment
drivers.line: Since Gemini and MSC's solo network (Feb 2025), owned tonnage is the weapon for market share.

banner: Fallacy of composition: each order is rational for one carrier, but together they make a supply wave that demand is unlikely to absorb in 2027–29 (Drewry: 'unavoidable' in 2027–28).
